newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AWB sells 68,500 t wheat in tender 30.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AWB sells 68,500 t wheat in tender 30.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Wednesday it sold 68,500 tonnes of wheat in its latest tender for domestic sales from its national pool.
Total bids were received for a record 794,500 tonnes of wheat, it said.
Bid prices increased significantly and the AWB also increased its reserve prices, it said.
These factors were all the result of increasing concern about crop prospects and El Nino drought effects on weather patterns over the remainder of the season, it said.
A total of 8,500 tonnes of old crop and 60,000 tonnes of new crop wheat was sold in the latest tender, the AWB said.
Old crop Australian Standard White (ASW) was sold at A$210 a tonne for Newcastle delivery and A$215 a tonne for Geelong delivery.
Old crop Australian Hard wheat was sold at A$225 a tonne for Geelong delivery.
New crop ASW was sold at A$207 a tonne for Newcastle delivery while Australian Hard was sold at A$222 a tonne for Newcastle delivery.
With substantially increased interest in the tender system, AWB merchandising general manager Ron Storey said tenders would now be held twice weekly.
